subject: bakery
title: Model Question Paper 3
meta: Time: 2 hours · Maximum marks: 40 · Modelled on the April 2026 NIOS paper (code 256)
instructions: All questions are compulsory and carry marks as indicated against each question.
Question 1: fifteen fill-in-the-blanks (1 mark each). Question 2: fifteen True/False statements (1 mark each). Question 3: four questions of 2½ marks each.
Questions from previous NIOS papers show the exam they appeared in.

sections.title: State whether the following statements are True or False.

questions.q: Milk is 100% water.
Only steel preparation tables are found in a bakery.
questions.answer: False. The table tops may also be made of marble.

questions.q: Pastry dough should be kneaded well to get crisp biscuits.
questions.answer: False. It should be handled as little as possible.

questions.q: Nuts used in egg white biscuits are generally ground finely.
Preheating of ovens is not necessary.
questions.answer: False. Cakes are baked in a preheated oven.

questions.q: Cakes made using the creaming method have no fat.
questions.answer: False. Fat is creamed with sugar.

questions.q: Glace icing can be prepared and kept for later use.
questions.answer: False. It sets very quickly and should be used immediately.

questions.q: A piping bag may be prepared with grease proof paper.
When dough is over rolled, the product becomes hard.
Kneading of dough helps in gluten formation.
Steps in bread loaf making are more than 12.
questions.answer: True. The recipe has about 20 steps.

questions.q: Croissants are made from leavened puff dough.

sections.title: Answer the following questions (five points each).

questions.q: Classify the ingredients used in a bakery according to their keeping quality, with examples.
questions.answer: (i) Non-perishable: kept for more than a month at room temperature, e.g. flour, sugar, salt, spices. (ii) Perishable: can be stored for a couple of days at the most at proper temperature, e.g. milk, cream, fresh fruits and vegetables, meat. (iii) Semi-perishable: need proper storage temperature but keep longer than perishables, e.g. butter and other fats, chocolates, eggs, opened tins.

questions.q: Name the four methods of making a cake and explain any two.
questions.answer: The four methods are rubbing-in, creaming, whisking and all-in-one. (i) Rubbing-in: chilled fat is cut small and rubbed into sieved flour until it looks like bread crumbs; used when the weight of fat is not more than half that of flour. (ii) All-in-one: all the ingredients are placed together in a bowl and beaten until smooth and creamy; used when quick preparation is wanted.

questions.q: What are the common faults in bread and their causes? Give any three.
questions.answer: (i) Too small a volume: too tight a dough, too little yeast, too little fermentation time or excess salt. (ii) Pale crust colour: excessive fermentation time, lack of salt, too high a dough temperature or excess yeast. (iii) Cracks in buns and rolls: under fermentation, under proofing or too high an oven temperature.

questions.q: What is a trial balance? State its objectives.
questions.answer: (i) A trial balance is a statement prepared with the balances of the ledger accounts. (ii) It checks the arithmetical accuracy of the journal entries and ledger postings; the debit and credit totals must be equal. (iii) It gives the balances of all ledger accounts at one place. (iv) It makes the staff careful and alert. (v) It helps in preparing the final accounts, the profit and loss account and the balance sheet.
